question.text: Mr. Vikram Rao, fund accountant at Vindhya Event-Driven Fund (Cat III), is drafting the PPM's 'required rate of return' framework for a merger-arbitrage sub-strategy. Per NISM Section 1.4, the required rate of return comprises which THREE components?

answer.text: Real risk-free rate + Expected inflation + Risk premium for uncertainty of future payments
Nominal risk-free rate + Beta + Illiquidity discount
Pure time value + Taxation adjustment + Market risk premium only (inflation is excluded as it is already captured in nominal)

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 1.4 states: 'Real risk-free rate + inflation adjustment + Risk premium adjustment = Required rate of return.' This is the three-component decomposition. The real risk-free rate compensates for postponing consumption (pure time value); inflation adjustment preserves purchasing power; risk premium compensates for uncertainty of future cashflows. The Trap: Option B mixes CAPM inputs (beta) with unrelated items. Option C lists performance metrics (Sharpe, alpha), not return components. Option D incorrectly excludes inflation — the chapter clearly has THREE additive components, not two. Cross-Exam Context: XV (RA) covers this decomposition for valuation; X-B (IA L2) uses it for financial planning; XXI-B (PM) uses it for portfolio construction. XIX-E frames it at the Cat III strategy-level — each sub-strategy (merger-arb, stat-arb, long-short) carries a different RISK-PREMIUM input but shares the same real-rate + inflation base. Manager's Pro-Tip: When sizing a merger-arb book at a Cat III fund, the required return on deal spreads must exceed nominal risk-free + deal-break premium (~2-4% depending on cash vs stock deal). Below that threshold, capital is better deployed in T-bills. Track this hurdle weekly — deals tightening below the hurdle should be unwound and capital recycled into fresh spreads with adequate compensation.
